passages.text: Again I looked, and I considered all the oppression taking place under the sun. I saw the tears of the oppressed, and they had no comforter; the power lay in the hands of their oppressors, and there was no comforter.
passages.sermon:
I looked again at the world under the sun.
I saw many people suffering from oppression.
I saw the tears of those who were oppressed.
No one comforted them.
Their oppressors held all the power.
No one comforted the oppressed.
passages.original: וְשַׁ֣בְתִּֽי אֲנִ֗י וָאֶרְאֶה֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ הָ֣עֲשֻׁקִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר נַעֲשִׂ֖ים תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ וְהִנֵּ֣ה׀ דִּמְעַ֣ת הָעֲשֻׁקִ֗ים וְאֵ֤ין לָהֶם֙ מְנַחֵ֔ם וּמִיַּ֤ד עֹֽשְׁקֵיהֶם֙ כֹּ֔חַ וְאֵ֥ין לָהֶ֖ם מְנַחֵֽם׃

passages.text: So I admired the dead, who had already died, above the living, who are still alive.
passages.sermon:
The writer is speaking about people who have died and people who are still alive.
The writer says he admires the dead.
These are the people who have already died.
He admires them more than the living.
The living are the people who are still alive now.
passages.original: וְשַׁבֵּ֧חַ אֲנִ֛י אֶת־ הַמֵּתִ֖ים שֶׁכְּבָ֣ר מֵ֑תוּ מִן־ הַ֣חַיִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֛ר הֵ֥מָּה חַיִּ֖ים עֲדֶֽנָה׃

passages.text: But better than both is he who has not yet existed, who has not seen the evil that is done under the sun.
passages.sermon:
The writer is observing life under the sun.
He sees much evil happening in the world.
He sees oppression and suffering.
He sees that some people have already died.
He sees that some people are still alive.
He says that someone who has never been born is better than both.
This person has not seen the evil done under the sun.
This person has not experienced the suffering in the world.
passages.original: וְטוֹב֙ מִשְּׁנֵיהֶ֔ם אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־ עֲדֶ֖ן לֹ֣א הָיָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־ רָאָה֙ אֶת־ הַמַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה הָרָ֔ע אֲשֶׁ֥ר נַעֲשָׂ֖ה תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃

passages.text: I saw that all labor and success spring from a man’s envy of his neighbor. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is Solomon, the wise king of Israel.
Solomon observed people’s work.
He saw all their efforts.
He saw all their skill in what they do.
He saw that people work hard because they envy their neighbors.
People want what others have.
This desire causes them to strive and compete.
Solomon said this is meaningless.
He said it is like chasing the wind.
passages.original: וְרָאִ֨יתִֽי אֲנִ֜י אֶת־ כָּל־ עָמָ֗ל וְאֵת֙ כָּל־ כִּשְׁר֣וֹן הַֽמַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה כִּ֛י הִ֥יא קִנְאַת־ אִ֖ישׁ מֵרֵעֵ֑הוּ גַּם־ זֶ֥ה הֶ֖בֶל וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ׃

passages.text: The fool folds his hands and consumes his own flesh.
passages.sermon:
A fool is a person who acts unwisely.
A fool folds his hands.
A fool does not work.
A fool consumes his own flesh.
A fool destroys himself by his laziness.
passages.original: הַכְּסִיל֙ חֹבֵ֣ק אֶת־ יָדָ֔יו וְאֹכֵ֖ל אֶת־ בְּשָׂרֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Better one handful with tranquility than two handfuls with toil and pursuit of the wind.
passages.sermon:
A person may work hard to gain much.
But it is better to have one handful with peace.
It is not good to have two handfuls with hard work and chasing after the wind.
Peace is better than endless striving.
passages.original: ט֕וֹב מְלֹ֥א כַ֖ף נָ֑חַת מִמְּלֹ֥א חָפְנַ֛יִם עָמָ֖ל וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ׃

passages.text: Again, I saw futility under the sun.
passages.sermon:
The writer is Solomon.  
Solomon is a wise king of Israel.  
Solomon looked at life on earth.  
Solomon saw that many things are futile.  
Solomon saw futility under the sun again.
passages.original: וְשַׁ֧בְתִּי אֲנִ֛י וָאֶרְאֶ֥ה הֶ֖בֶל תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃

passages.text: There is a man all alone, without even a son or brother. And though there is no end to his labor, his eyes are still not content with his wealth: “For whom do I toil and bereave my soul of enjoyment?” This too is futile—a miserable task.
passages.sermon:
There is a man who is completely alone.
He has no son.
He has no brother.
He works without end.
He never stops his labor.
He keeps working, but he is never satisfied with his wealth.
He asks himself, “For whom am I working?”
He says, “Why do I deprive myself of good things?”
This is also meaningless.
This is a miserable task.
passages.original: יֵ֣שׁ אֶחָד֩ וְאֵ֨ין שֵׁנִ֜י גַּ֣ם בֵּ֧ן וָאָ֣ח אֵֽין־ ל֗וֹ וְאֵ֥ין קֵץ֙ לְכָל־ עֲמָל֔וֹ גַּם־ עֵינָיו לֹא־ תִשְׂבַּ֣ע עֹ֑שֶׁר וּלְמִ֣י׀ אֲנִ֣י עָמֵ֗ל וּמְחַסֵּ֤ר אֶת־ נַפְשִׁי֙ מִטּוֹבָ֔ה גַּם־ זֶ֥ה הֶ֛בֶל וְעִנְיַ֥ן רָ֖ע הֽוּא׃

passages.text: Two are better than one, because they have a good return for their labor.
passages.sermon:
Two people work together.
They are better than one person alone.
They gain a good reward from their work.
Working together brings greater benefit.
passages.original: טוֹבִ֥ים הַשְּׁנַ֖יִם מִן־ הָאֶחָ֑ד אֲשֶׁ֧ר יֵשׁ־ לָהֶ֛ם שָׂכָ֥ר ט֖וֹב בַּעֲמָלָֽם׃

passages.text: For if one falls down, his companion can lift him up; but pity the one who falls without another to help him up!
passages.sermon:
This passage describes two people who work or live together.
If one person falls down, his companion can help him get up.
But if a person falls and has no one with him, no one can help him rise.
It is sad for the person who falls alone, because he has no one to help him.
passages.original: כִּ֣י אִם־ יִפֹּ֔לוּ הָאֶחָ֖ד יָקִ֣ים אֶת־ חֲבֵר֑וֹ וְאִ֣יל֗וֹ הָֽאֶחָד֙ שֶׁיִּפּ֔וֹל וְאֵ֥ין שֵׁנִ֖י לַהֲקִימֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Again, if two lie down together, they will keep warm; but how can one keep warm alone?
passages.sermon: Two people can lie down together.\r\nThey will keep warm.\r\nOne person alone cannot keep warm.
passages.original: גַּ֛ם אִם־ יִשְׁכְּב֥וּ שְׁנַ֖יִם וְחַ֣ם לָהֶ֑ם וּלְאֶחָ֖ד אֵ֥יךְ יֵחָֽם׃

passages.text: And though one may be overpowered, two can resist. Moreover, a cord of three strands is not quickly broken.
passages.sermon:
One person may be attacked.
Two people can stand together against the attacker.
A cord with three strands is strong.
A cord with three strands does not break easily.
passages.original: וְאִֽם־ יִתְקְפוֹ֙ הָאֶחָ֔ד הַשְּׁנַ֖יִם יַעַמְד֣וּ נֶגְדּ֑וֹ וְהַחוּט֙ הַֽמְשֻׁלָּ֔שׁ לֹ֥א בִמְהֵרָ֖ה יִנָּתֵֽק׃

passages.text: Better is a poor but wise youth than an old but foolish king who no longer knows how to take a warning.
passages.sermon:
A poor youth can be wise.
A wise youth is better than a king who is old and foolish.
An old king may not listen to warnings anymore.
A wise youth is better than a king who does not accept advice.
passages.original: ט֛וֹב יֶ֥לֶד מִסְכֵּ֖ן וְחָכָ֑ם מִמֶּ֤לֶךְ זָקֵן֙ וּכְסִ֔יל אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹא־ יָדַ֥ע לְהִזָּהֵ֖ר עֽוֹד׃

passages.text: For the youth has come from the prison to the kingship, though he was born poor in his own kingdom.
passages.sermon:
A young man was born poor in his own kingdom.
He lived in poverty from birth.
He was not born into wealth or power.
He came out of prison.
He became king after leaving prison.
He rose from a low and difficult place to a high position.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ מִבֵּ֥ית הָסוּרִ֖ים יָצָ֣א לִמְלֹ֑ךְ כִּ֛י גַּ֥ם בְּמַלְכוּת֖וֹ נוֹלַ֥ד רָֽשׁ׃

passages.text: I saw that all who lived and walked under the sun followed this second one, the youth who succeeded the king.
passages.sermon:
I saw all the people who live on earth.
They walk and act under the sun.
They followed the second youth.
This youth took the place of the king.
passages.original: רָאִ֙יתִי֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ הַ֣חַיִּ֔ים הַֽמְהַלְּכִ֖ים תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ עִ֚ם הַיֶּ֣לֶד הַשֵּׁנִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲמֹ֖ד תַּחְתָּֽיו׃

passages.text: There is no limit to all the people who were before them. Yet the successor will not be celebrated by those who come even later. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
passages.sermon:
There is no end to all the people who lived before.
Many people came before the new king.
Those who come later will not rejoice in the new king.
This is also meaningless.
This is like chasing the wind.
passages.original: אֵֽין־ קֵ֣ץ לְכָל־ הָעָ֗ם לְכֹ֤ל אֲשֶׁר־ הָיָה֙ לִפְנֵיהֶ֔ם גַּ֥ם הָאַחֲרוֹנִ֖ים לֹ֣א יִשְׂמְחוּ־ ב֑וֹ כִּֽי־ גַם־ זֶ֥ה הֶ֖בֶל וְרַעְי֥וֹן רֽוּחַ׃
